at s = 15 mV. The paper reports one experimenter above 15 mV without naming which or by how much; the 4 forks tolerate a single-lab spread of only 16.0 to 24.5 mV, and one lab (hot_pink) appears in 3 of them (NONE survive if any single lab's spread is 30 mV). Full sweep 4/15/20/23 forks at s=15/10/7.5/5 mV of 36 testable lab pairs (9 of 11 labs machine-read from Fig. 5); the spread values were chosen AFTER the figure was read (error bars below the raster resolution), so they are NOT pre-registered. READ FROM A FIGURE; reproduces a spread Tesch 2023 already reported, NOT a new finding; alkaline Ni-Co oxide, not Lila's; loop plan_only (OERSIM electrolyte is OER13 = 0.1 M NaOH+0.25 M Na2SO4, pH 13, not 1 M KOH; no run faked). The fork COUNT is not robust; what IS robust is rr_central_range.
locked.value: round-robin known-answer forks detected (count NOT robust)

locked.qualifier: ROBUST — the inter-lab central-value range at 10 mA cm-2, read from Fig. 5 of Tesch 2023 (CC BY 3.0); the paper itself reports this inter-lab spread. (The per-pair fork count is NOT robust: 0 to 4 at s=15 mV; see rr_forks.)
locked.value: round-robin inter-lab central range read from figure (ROBUST)

honest_nulls: No real cross-source fork found in public data. Reason: public data rarely holds, together, the SAME entity measured by MULTIPLE sources under STATED conditions with STATED per-row uncertainty.

Biology fork-testing is UNTESTABLE: no public enzyme-kinetics database (CatLog-27k / EnzyArena / CatPred-DB) carries a per-row uncertainty, and none has same-source replicate structure for a clean noise null.
The cross-field result is a matcher-correctness test on AUTHORED graphs, not a discovery.
